items.topic: Which scenario does this work target?
items.context: No scope field is set on spec.json. Identifying the target scenario is required before implementation planning can proceed. Based on the item name and available scenarios, here are likely candidates.

options.label: scenarios/swarm-manager
options.rationale: Most likely if this is about testing/improving the backlog scope field functionality within swarm-manager itself.

options.label: scenarios/agent-manager
options.rationale: If the scope test relates to agent sandbox scoping and acceptance boundaries.

options.label: No specific scenario (infrastructure/cross-cutting)
options.rationale: If this is a platform-level concern that spans multiple scenarios.

items.topic: What file paths are expected to change?
items.context: Both acceptance_allow and acceptance_deny are missing from spec.json. Once the target scenario is known, we need to define the expected change boundaries for sandbox scoping and post-execution review.

options.label: Broad: scenarios/<target>/**
options.rationale: Allow changes anywhere in the target scenario. Appropriate for large features or new scenarios.

options.label: Targeted subdirectories only
options.rationale: Restrict to specific subdirectories (e.g., api/internal/backlog/**). Appropriate for focused changes.

options.label: Defer until scope is decided
options.rationale: Wait for d1 and d2 answers before defining acceptance boundaries.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify custom acceptance_allow and acceptance_deny patterns.

items.notes: Pre-selected C since this depends on decisions d1 and d2.

items.context: Currently set to priority 5 (mid-range). Should this be adjusted based on the actual scope of work?

items.text: The existing plan.md contains all 13 mandatory sections but every section is marked <!-- TBD -->. No archive materials were provided. The plan cannot be meaningfully populated until the purpose and scope are defined through this workshop round.

The backlog system supports scope, acceptance_allow, and acceptance_deny fields on spec.json. These are used for sandbox overlay mounts, post-execution review targeting, and change boundary validation. Setting these after d2 is answered will improve execution safety.
